guide.title: Guide
guide.intro: A short guide by task. Open it any time with F1 or from the command palette.

addDocs.title: Add documents
addDocs.body: Drop PDF files or a folder into the window, or use Add PDF in the Library or in To review (Alt+2). The app reads titles and metadata, files them in your library and shows what it found for you to confirm. The Activity chip, at the top right, follows the scan: See the report lists new, changed, moved and missing files. Your originals are never changed.

tags.title: Organize with tags and projects
tags.body: In the Library select documents (with the box at the left of each row): the bar that replaces the filters offers Tags, Project and Claude. Tags are managed from Manage tags, in the Library ⋯ menu. You can undo any change with Undo, in the top bar, or Ctrl+Z; Redo is Ctrl+Y, in the History and in the command palette. The search box at the top finds text, titles and authors (? shows the syntax); the sparkle button searches with Claude.

read.title: Read and annotate
read.body: Double-click a document (or press Enter) to open it in the reader; Shift+Enter opens its card. Select text to highlight or underline it and to add a note. Notes, highlights and citations are saved in your library folder and travel with it. For now highlights stay in the app only: writing into the PDFs is not on yet. Reader tools use single keys. At the first start after the update Research Lab re-checks highlights that were saved misplaced, in the background and without opening the documents; those it cannot place stay in the reader's To check group.

chat.title: Ask Claude
chat.body: Open Claude from the sidebar (Ctrl+J) and use the command palette for ready-made requests. Claude only sees documents in folders you have enabled for it, and you can preview exactly what is sent before you send. You can choose to use your Claude Code login or an API key. Test the connection costs about $0.001 and sends no documents. Change account opens a Claude Code window; then come back and press I'm done, check. Signing out of Claude Code also applies in the terminal.

network.title: Explore the map
network.body: The Map section (Alt+5) draws documents, authors and topics as a map and as a graph, so you can find clusters and related work. It is built from your own library and rebuilt when needed.

export.title: Export and connect other tools
export.body: Export a project or a selection as a second brain (notes with links) from the command palette. In the settings you can also start a local MCP server so other tools can read your library.

backup.title: Back up your library
backup.body: In the settings choose a destination folder and press Back up now, or turn on the automatic backup. A backup can be verified and restored as a new library at any time. Secrets such as API keys are never saved in a backup. Settings save by themselves: search them from the box at the top left (Ctrl+,). Technical options are in Developer / Advanced. On first start the app uses the system language (Italian or English); libraries are managed with Manage libraries…
